newsitem.title: USA: Cool weather, scattered showers seen in US Midwest.
newsitem.headline: Cool weather, scattered showers seen in US Midwest.

text.p: Cool weather and scattered showers should be common across the U.S. Midwest during the Independence Day weekend and early next week, meteorologists said.

Severe thunderstorms that moved throught the eastern Midwest overnight Wednesday and early Thursday brought less than 0.5 inch rain to Michigan, Indiana and Ohio, but spawned damaging high winds and tornadoes.
"There is no excessive heat in the cornbelt indicated by the American or European (weather) models," said Fred Gesser, meteorologist with Weather Express Inc.

Gesser said southeast Nebraska, southwest Iowa, northwest Missouri and northeast Kansas should receive 0.5 to 1.5 inches of rain Thursday and Friday, before moving to the southeast and "fizzling out."
Scattered showers, possibly 40 percent coverage, of 0.25 to 1.5 inches were likely across southern Illinois, southern Indiana, Ohio and Kentucky Friday and Saturday, he said.

Scattered showers should occur throughout much of next week in the Midwest. Even the dry areas in central Illinois may receive some light showers Sunday, said Joel Burgio, meteorologist with Weather Services Inc.
In June, the area around Springfield, Ill., received less than 50 percent of its normal moisture, Burgio said.
